subject: zoology_2
question_text: Write a note on Addison's disease and Cushing's syndrome.

verification.note: Sourced from 'My Baby Bullet-Q — Senior Inter Zoology' (Star-Q Pass Track Series, Sri Publishers, 2022), book p.34, SAQ 24. The printed exam years are the book's claim, reproduced here as appearances. Zoology-II holds only ONE source book in the corpus, so the two-book union check is structurally impossible for this card; 'not checked' does NOT mean 'checked and clean'. The mark split is our reading of the question and is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

steps.label: Addison's disease
steps.why: Glucocorticoids are the hormones that let the body cope with stress, so too little of them leaves a person unable to respond to it.
common_mistakes: Naming the adrenal medulla. Glucocorticoids come from the cortex.
steps.memory_tip: Addison is 'a' for absent: too little glucocorticoid.
lines: It is due to hyposecretion of

steps.label: Its symptoms
steps.why: Without glucocorticoids the body cannot mobilise its stores, so weight and strength fall away.
common_mistakes: Giving weight gain. In Addison's disease weight is lost.
Leaving out the darkening of the skin.
steps.memory_tip: Weight down, pressure down, skin darker.
steps.margin_note: List the symptoms. Each one is a tick.
lines: The symptoms are loss of weight, muscle
and darkening of the skin colour.
The patient cannot respond to stress.

steps.label: Cushing's syndrome
steps.why: Too much of the same hormone drives the body the other way, storing fat and raising blood sugar.
steps.memory_tip: Cushing is the cushion: fat is laid down.
lines: It is due to hypersecretion of

steps.label: Its symptoms
steps.why: Fat is moved to the trunk, face and back while the limbs waste, which gives the shape the disease is known by.
common_mistakes: Giving weight loss. In Cushing's syndrome weight is gained.
Leaving out the moon face and buffalo hump.
steps.memory_tip: Moon face, buffalo hump, thin arms and legs.
steps.margin_note: The named signs are what the examiner ticks.
lines: The symptoms are spindle like arms and
legs, a round moon face, a buffalo hump on
the back, a pendulous abdomen, poor wound

insider_note: The two diseases are opposite ends of one hormone. Say hyposecretion for one and hypersecretion for the other in the first line of each — that single word carries the mark.
